filename: Bayesian Deep Learning for Convective Initiation Nowcasting Uncertainty Estimation 2026.pdf
title: Bayesian Deep Learning for Convective Initiation Nowcasting Uncertainty Estimation
venue: Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems
testbed_rationale: The study develops statistical nowcasting classification models for 0-1-h convective initiation from satellite imagery rather than climate/Earth system model physics parameterization or simulation emulation.
pain_points: Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) require optimizing twice as many weights as deterministic networks and struggle to converge to optimal solutions without informed priors like MOPED.
Undersampling the majority non-CI class to balance data caused degraded generalization in underrepresented regimes such as broad clear-sky and anvil cloud regions.
Satellite and radar observations cannot resolve subkilometer scale processes (<1 km) critical for CI, including small cumulus clouds and fine differential topography.
Models exhibit significantly lower skill during nighttime/early morning hours due to inherent challenges in forecasting nocturnal convection.
extraction_notes: The underlying dataset processing methodology originated from Fan et al. (2024), but the curated dataset DOI (10.26208/6Y59-0R80) and GitHub repository (CIUQ) are provided directly in the data availability statement.
